content: This medication is a combination product containing conjugated estrogens and bazedoxifene, which is used by women with a uterus to alleviate menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, and to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis) after menopause. Conjugated estrogens are hormones that help reduce menopausal symptoms caused by the body's decreased estrogen production. Bazedoxifene, while not a hormone, acts like estrogen in certain parts of the body as a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM). Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. To minimize stomach upset, you may take it with food or immediately after a meal. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them. For maximum benefit, take this medication regularly at the same time each day. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it may increase your blood pressure and, in rare cases, cause serious problems such as blood clots (e.g., heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs). Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to conjugated estrogens, bazedoxifene, or any other ingredients in the product. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco, as it increases the risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions also increase the risk of blood clots. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin (melasma), which can worsen with sunlight exposure. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. Estrogens can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. It is unknown if bazedoxifene passes into breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test, blood clotting tests, thyroid tests), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes through lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving puzzles) to help prevent dementia. Promote healthy bones by increasing weight-bearing exercise, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol, and consuming a well-balanced diet with adequate calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Once the foil pouch is opened, the U.S. product expires after 60 days, and the Canadian product expires after 45 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Estrogens, whether used alone or with another hormone (progestin), have rarely caused very serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone treatment with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). The bazedoxifene in this product may help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, with or without progestin, increase the risk of breast/ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The risk of serious side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration necessary. Discuss the use of this medication with your doctor and check with them regularly (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if you still need to take it. If you will be taking this medication long-term, regular complete physical exams (e.g., annually) should be conducted as directed by your doctor.
